questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good school, English as spoken language, architecture of the city and size of city

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy - you get loads of information and several reminders hereof just follow these

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: International check in

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I got a PG flat right on campus - even though I was UG - really good location and if if they tell you that "they might not have something available" they will - you just gotta have patience and wait until like 2 weeks before (end of august)

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Self-catered

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Really good location and if if they tell you that "they might not have something available" they will - you just gotta have patience and wait until like 2 weeks before (end of august)- Be REALLY aware of your room and flat at move in and report any issues immediately otherwise this will become a problem later on! We had a lot of issues with water in general, but they fixed them eventually.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They often come into your apartment both for cleaning and maintenance - just something to be aware of if you really value personal space then maybe look for private accommodation instead.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They will become available online and then when you are here it is pretty easy to change by sending in requests

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Your "personal" advisor

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Yes, I got all that I wanted and changed one class in the first week as it was too introductory - a first year class

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pick courses that sound interesting but don't stress too much about your first choices. Pick from 2 year and above unless you wanna be kind of bored or do a whole other subject than your own

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was at level with home - more explaining of theoretical work and the assignments are more based on internet-research than qualitative methods and shorter. It is pretty stressfull with midterms on top of the regular work load - they expect you to read and do 3 essays.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Different structure with tutorials - very small classes and lecture - very large classes
It was more important to read, but less mandatory reading - be beware of how the different classes value the recommended and further readings

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Ritual and religion, Anthropological theory and social life and climate change

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: social life and climate change was pretty interesting as well as ritual and religion

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of options for everything

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Pick something and try it

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The highlands are beautiful and go to north Berwick

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Get their contact the first time you talk and ask them to go for a coffee or drink

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: A bit more formal in the school system

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people  - they are soo nice but talk really fast, and the city landscape

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Relax and enjoy all the new things, go to the open office hours and talk to the professors if you are struggling with anything

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do NOT spend every weekend at the library, go a couple of hours a day and explore in the weekends

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the new people and living in the most beautiful city

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The academics here are very intense and take up a lot of time - but you will have time to enjoy everthing else - you are all in the same boat

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
